**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The repair tightened the citations so they point only at the sections that *would* host an audit right rather than at near-hits that could be misread as audit language:

- **Cited as the locus of absence:** § 3 use restrictions (p0029, p0035, p0039) and § 20 general matters (p0134). § 3 imposes substantive use limits only — no verification, reporting or records mechanism attaches to them.
- **Coverage confirmed:** § 2 grant, § 14 confidentiality, § 17 term/termination and § 20 all read; searches for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, records, access, premises, remote, report, books, right to enter* all return nothing relevant.
- **Near-hits expressly excluded from the rule:** p0114 (escrow examination) runs in our favour; p0118 is a single post-termination destruction certificate, not a recurring audit and not system access.

On the failed deterministic check, I have kept the compliant status and recorded in the rationale why the signal is spurious: the "audit frequency limited" pattern cannot match where no audit clause exists. Inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters purely to satisfy the regex would manufacture an audit right against Sparkling that Garman does not currently have — the opposite of the rule's intent. If Garman later proposes any verification or usage-reporting clause, the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no access to our systems) should be inserted into § 3 at that point.
